item.title: CPU Floating Point Division Latency vs Multiplication Speed Explained
item.description:
“CPU Floating Point Division Latency vs Multiplication Speed Explained”

A frequently debated topic in low-level performance programming centers on the relative execution speeds of floating-point division (/) compared to multiplication (*) on modern Central Processing Units (CPUs). While multiplication is often executed in just one or two clock cycles, division consistently exhibits significantly higher latency. Why does this fundamental arithmetic difference persist in high-speed silicon?

item.title: Why is the x86 LOOP instruction slow on modern CPUs
item.description:
“Why is the x86 LOOP instruction slow on modern CPUs”

The LOOP instruction in x86 assembly has a peculiar reputation for being significantly slower on modern processors compared to its earlier counterparts. While on processors like the 8088 and 80286 it was often faster than a DEC CX followed by a JNZ, its performance on later architectures, especially those with advanced pipelining and out-of-order execution, has noticeably degraded. What architectural shifts and design decisions led to this performance disparity?
